summary.tldr: Requires certain parties to publish diversity information and directs the Chief Electoral Officer to collect and report demographic data on candidates and contestants.
what_it_does: Requires certain registered parties, those whose candidates won at least 2% of valid votes nationwide or 5% in the districts where they ran, to post candidate selection rules, diversity programs, progress reports, and annual updates on their websites.

Requires those parties to post plans and rules about nominating women candidates, including target numbers or percentages, rules for some by-elections or when a sitting MP does not run again, and progress toward those targets.
Requires parties with no diversity program, plan, or rule to post a statement explaining why and, if any, when they plan to adopt one, plus contact information for questions.

Gives the Chief Electoral Officer power to collect voluntary self-identification questionnaires from candidates, nomination contestants, and leadership contestants, then publish anonymized reports on demographic information after general elections, by-elections, and leadership contests.
Extends the non-voluntary deregistration process so the Chief Electoral Officer can act if a party or officer fails to meet the new public disclosure duties.
